lines.watchItem: Cloud buyers keep raising their build budgets and their signed-but-undelivered order books keep growing, so leading-edge wafer planning faces a strong pull rather than a fading one. The open question is how long that pull holds.

Advanced packaging, not wafer output, is what caps how many accelerators can ship: capacity is booked out at 52 to 78 week waits even as output climbs toward 130,000 wafers a month and the shortfall narrows from about 20% to about 10%. The thing to watch is whether packaging keeps easing while memory stays the tighter limit.

Rival packaging suppliers now quote 26 to 39 weeks against 52 to 78 weeks here, other assembly houses are adding capacity, and one large accelerator maker is weighing a move of some next-generation output to a competitor's packaging. That waiting-time gap is where packaging share can leak.

Three customers hold more than 85% of advanced-packaging output, the largest at roughly 60%, and they have booked over half of the coming expansion. Any one of them slowing orders leaves capacity that is hard to refill.

Chips designed for a single cloud buyer are growing about 45% this year against 16% for standard accelerators, while the leading accelerator maker's share tracks down from 87% toward a projected 75% and a second merchant vendor books gigawatt-scale commitments. The leading-node customer base is broadening away from one dominant buyer.

The second merchant vendor holds only about a tenth of advanced-packaging output and has to split it between its server processors and its accelerators, so each processor it packages costs it an accelerator. That trade-off shapes how much of its growth can reach the leading node.

Foundry gross margin reached 67.7% with revenue up 36% and the full-year growth outlook raised, while demand spreading into custom chips, networking and power parts fills capacity across both older and newer nodes. Pricing power currently sits with the constrained suppliers rather than the buyers.

A growing slice of accelerator demand rests on the seller's own credit and on borrowed money: one vendor backstops customer purchases covering roughly 210,000 chips at smaller clouds, and the largest cloud buyer funded its quarter with equity and notes while posting its first negative free cash flow. That is the part of the demand signal most exposed to a reversal.
